messages:
Anne: Quick helm templating question — trying to conditionally add an envFrom secretRef but template rendering ends up producing an empty name and k8s rejects it. Snippet below, any obvious bug?

```yaml
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.redis.secretName }}
```

When `secretName` is empty we want no envFrom entry. I wrapped it in an `if` but still saw a blank `name:` field in the rendered manifest. :thinking:

Devon: Can you paste the surrounding template? Common gotcha: values from YAML can be empty string vs null. `if .Values.redis.secretName` will be truthy for non-empty, but if the value is the empty string you may still get interpolation. Try `with` or explicit empty-string check.

Devon: Example that usually works:

```tpl
{{- with .Values.redis.secretName }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ . }}
{{- end }}
```

Marco: `with` treats zero-values as empty so it should skip when the value is ""? IIRC `with` will skip for empty string, but if values.yaml includes `secretName: ""` sometimes the chart renderer still prints blank? worth testing.

Linda: If you want to be explicit, check for non-empty string:

```tpl
{{- if ne (trim .Values.redis.secretName) "" }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.redis.secretName }}
{{- end }}
```

Linda: Another pattern is to use `default` to coerce to nil: `{{- $s := default nil .Values.redis.secretName }}` then `if $s` — but `default nil` is tricky depending on how Helm/Go templates handle types.

ci-bot: chart-lint: pipeline passed for `charts/platform` (chart v0.3.7) :white_check_mark:

Anne: Good tips. My values.yaml currently comes from our infra repo where CI generates `secretName: ""` for optional secrets, so that explains it. I like the `trim` check.

Devon: Also consider whether you want `envFrom` at all. If you only need a couple keys, explicit `env` entries are safer (no accidental env pollution). For platform shared charts we usually prefer explicit keys unless the secret is small and well-scoped.

Marco: I pushed a quick commit to `infra/test-values.yaml` setting `redis.secretName: null` so we can see nil vs empty string behaviour in the renderer. Will wait for CI and link the render output.

Linda: FYI, if the secret might not exist in-cluster and you want to gate on existence, you can use `lookup`:

```tpl
{{- $s := lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace .Values.redis.secretName }}
{{- if $s }}
# safe to reference
{{- end }}
```

Anne: Perfect. I'll open a tiny PR with the `trim` guard + a comment explaining why, and include a rendered manifest in the PR so reviewers don't hit the blank-name error. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Devon: Thanks — ping us when it's up and we can quick-review.
